title: Adaptive Reservation Pilot -> Operational Handbook & Canary Sequence
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Objective: Run a targeted pilot that converts the adaptive reservation experiment into an operational runbook for Dedicated pools. Scope: (1) define capacity slicing rules that let high-value customers burst without violating SLO corridors; (2) specify canary sequence and telemetry for safe rollouts; (3) create Console toggles and API flags for fast rollback and manual override; (4) produce runbook pages for oncall and SRE with play-by-play actions and economics checks. Exclusions: not covering cross-region warm-pool choreography in this pilot; VPC/private network changes will be handled in follow-up ticket. Motivation: current reserved pools can be underutilized in off-peak windows while sudden demand spikes cause degraded latency. Adaptive reservations aim to reduce wasted cost while maintaining per-customer latency and throughput SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot runbook drafted and reviewed by SRE, Runtime, and Console leads
Canary sequence defined with at least three staged slices and explicit success/failure metrics
Console UI mock for 'adaptive reservation' toggle + manual override documented and signed off by design
Experiment executed on two Dedicated pools for 48 hours with telemetry exported to dashboards and cost delta calculated
Rollback & escape-hatch procedures validated in a tabletop run with oncall (incidents simulated)
Post-pilot decision made: promote to runbook + rollout schedule or iterate on policy thresholds

rollout_steps: Step 0: Instrumentation — Runtime emits 'capacity_slice' and 'slice_health' events; Console can surface slice status
Step 1: Internal Canary — enable Pilot mode on a non-customer pool for 6 hours, validate prewarm success rate >= 90% and median latency within SLO
Step 2: Limited Customer Canary — opt-in two low-risk enterprise accounts (consent obtained) for 24 hours; monitor cost delta and customer KPIs
Step 3: Gradual Expansion — expand to 10% of Dedicated pools across two regions, keep guardrails and automatic rollback triggers active
Step 4: Tabletop & Runbook Finalization — run a simulated outage; finalize handoff docs for oncall and account managers
Step 5: Post-Pilot Review — consolidate metrics, finance impact, and decide on 'Enforced' rollout or additional iteration
failure_modes_and_mitigations: Failure: Prewarm fails frequently -> Mitigation: automatically revert affected customers to static reservation policy and create alert to engineering
Failure: Unexpected cost spike -> Mitigation: enforce hard cost ceiling per-pool and trigger immediate rollback to last stable reservation state
Failure: Telemetry gap -> Mitigation: block pilot progression until instrumentation gaps fixed; fallback to sampling traces for retrospective analysis
